title: Authentication Mechanism Strength Comparison
description: Interactive p5.js infographic comparing seven authentication mechanisms across phishing resistance, usability, and account-recovery ease, with dropdowns to switch threat model and highlight recommendations for consumers, enterprise, or high-value accounts.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity
chapter_title: "Human Security: Identity, Authentication, and Social Engineering"

learningObjectives: Judge which authentication mechanism is appropriate for a given threat model and user population.
Justify the choice using phishing resistance, usability, and recovery cost as criteria.
Explain why origin-bound credentials (FIDO2, passkeys) resist phishing that codes and push prompts do not.
educational.prerequisites: Familiarity with passwords and the idea of a second factor.

controls: Select: threat model (opportunistic credential stuffing vs targeted spear-phishing)
Select: highlight mechanisms recommended for consumers / enterprise / high-value accounts
pedagogical.assessment: Students pick a mechanism for a scenario and defend it against both threat models.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing any second factor is equally phishing-resistant.
Treating usability and security as always in conflict (passkeys score high on both).
